planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall through early spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; Blackcomb was bred in British Columbia for immunity to white pine blister rust and strong frost tolerance.

directions: Blackcomb is a black currant selection from a British Columbia breeding program that targeted immunity to white pine blister rust alongside strong cold and frost tolerance, making it useful where that disease threatens nearby white pines. Grow in full sun to partial shade in moist, fertile, well-drained soil, spacing bushes generously for airflow through the dense growth. Fruit forms mainly on one- and two-year-old wood, so remove the oldest third of canes each winter to keep the bush renewing itself and cropping heavily. Harvest clusters once berries darken fully in midsummer, since black currants continue to sweeten for several days after they first color.

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall through early spring in rich, moisture-retentive soil; Tahsis was released alongside Blackcomb for blister-rust immunity and frost tolerance during bloom.

directions: Tahsis was released alongside Blackcomb from the same British Columbia breeding program, selected for immunity to white pine blister rust and for tolerating hard frosts during bloom. Plant dormant bushes in early spring or fall in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun to light shade, and mulch to keep roots cool through summer. Because black currants crop on recent wood, prune out roughly a third of the oldest stems every dormant season to encourage vigorous new growth. The glossy black berries ripen in midsummer and suit jam, cordial, and baking better than fresh eating given their tart intensity.

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall or early spring; Tisel is a Polish Research Institute of Horticulture release from around 2000 bred for dependable Central European cropping.

directions: Tisel is a Polish black currant cultivar released around 2000 from the Research Institute of Horticulture's breeding program, developed for reliable cropping under Central European growing conditions. Set out dormant bushes in fall or early spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants for good air circulation to limit mildew and leaf spot. Prune annually in winter, removing older canes so the bush continually replaces itself with young, productive wood. Expect clusters of aromatic, dark berries in midsummer, well suited to syrup, jam, and juice.
sources: Wikipedia: Blackcurrant (Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program)

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall through early spring; Tiben was released in the same 2000 cohort as Tisel from Poland's Research Institute of Horticulture.

directions: Tiben was released in the same 2000 cohort as Tisel from the Polish Research Institute of Horticulture's black currant breeding program, bred for dependable production in Central European orchards. Grow in full sun to partial shade in cool, moist, humus-rich soil, planting dormant bushes from fall through early spring. Like most black currants, Tiben fruits best on younger wood, so thin out the oldest canes each winter to maintain vigor and berry size. Harvest the richly flavored black berries once fully colored in midsummer for jam, cordial, or home winemaking.
sources: Wikipedia: Blackcurrant (Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program)

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall or early spring; Ores is a 2005 Polish Research Institute of Horticulture release alongside Ruben and Tines.

directions: Ores is a Polish black currant cultivar introduced in 2005 from the same Research Institute of Horticulture program that produced Tisel, Tiben, Ruben, and Tines, aimed at improving yield and reliability for growers in cooler climates. Plant dormant bushes in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, spacing them widely enough to keep foliage dry and reduce disease pressure. Remove the oldest wood each dormant season, since black currants crop most heavily on one- and two-year-old canes. Berries ripen in clusters through midsummer, carrying the intense, musky-sweet black currant flavor prized for preserves and juice.
sources: Wikipedia: Blackcurrant (Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program)

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall or early spring; Ruben is part of the 2005 release group from Poland's Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program.

directions: Ruben is part of the 2005 release group from Poland's Research Institute of Horticulture black currant breeding program, developed alongside Ores and Tines for improved productivity under Central European conditions. Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting dormant bushes out in fall or early spring and spacing them for good airflow. Annual winter pruning that removes the oldest third of canes keeps the bush renewing itself and producing full-sized fruit. The dark, strongly aromatic berries ripen in midsummer and are typically used for jam, cordial, and juice rather than fresh eating.
sources: Wikipedia: Blackcurrant (Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program)

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall or early spring; Tines was released in 2005 from the same Polish breeding program as Ores and Ruben.

directions: Tines was released in 2005 from the same Polish Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program as Ores and Ruben, broadening the range of productive black currant cultivars available to Central European growers. Grow in full sun to partial shade in cool, fertile, well-drained soil, planting dormant stock from fall through early spring. Because fruit forms mainly on younger wood, prune out the oldest canes every winter to sustain vigorous cropping. Clusters of dark, tart berries ripen in midsummer and suit jam, syrup, and baking best.
sources: Wikipedia: Blackcurrant (Research Institute of Horticulture breeding program)

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes fall or early spring; Vertti is a Finnish green-fruited black currant type known locally as viherherukka ('greencurrant').

directions: Vertti is a green-fruited black currant cultivar grown in Finland, where such pale, milder, sweeter selections are known locally as viherherukka, or greencurrants, distinct from the dark, intensely tart standard black currant. It shares the hardy, cold-climate constitution typical of black currants bred for Nordic growing conditions, tolerating very cold winters once established. Plant dormant bushes in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune out the oldest canes each winter to keep the shrub productive. The pale green berries ripen in midsummer and, being milder and sweeter than typical black currants, are enjoyed fresh as well as cooked.
